skill.name: compose-doctor
skill.description: Diagnose an existing Goldsky Compose app with failing tasks, crashloops, missed events, cron not firing, HTTP 500s, wallet or gas sponsorship failures, missing secrets, bundler errors, manifest validation failures, or esbuild failures. Use when an app is named alongside a problem involving goldsky compose, including 'No bundler provider available', named wallets without a private key in local dev, and 'Transaction Receipt failed with status'. Load /compose first; inspect status, logs, secrets, and wallets to find the cause. New apps belong in /compose; reference-only lookups use skills/compose/references/. Use /secrets for secret management and /auth-setup for login. Turbo, Mirror, Subgraph, and Edge issues have separate skills.
skill.summary: Diagnose existing Goldsky Compose apps using status, logs, run history, deployed source, secret names, and wallet information.
skill.author: goldsky-io

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown formatting, diagnostic examples, or scoped cache maintenance rather than malicious execution, credential theft, or reconnaissance. Confirmed risks include forced deployment, forced cleanup, and automatic pausing; a separate semantic finding covers automatic secret changes and redeployment without explicit approval. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection; the skill explicitly treats logs as untrusted.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:169 recommends bypassing a major API version compatibility safeguard.
remediation.suggestion: Check compatibility and migration requirements first; require explicit approval before any forced deployment.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:170 adds a force flag to cleanup without reviewing affected resources.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the cleanup scope, preserve required state, and obtain explicit approval before running forced cleanup.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:192 directs pausing apps before investigation without an approval requirement.
remediation.suggestion: Start with read-only checks; confirm the target and obtain approval for any pause that interrupts task execution.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:130 permits automatic secret changes, manifest edits, and redeployment during diagnosis.
remediation.suggestion: Separate diagnosis from remediation; present changes, verify the project and environment, and request approval before applying them.

content.value_statement: Existing Compose apps can fail because of task errors, missing secrets, wallet settings, or deployment mismatches. This skill guides evidence-based diagnosis and proposes targeted fixes.
actual_capabilities: Guide authentication checks, app identification, and status inspection through the Goldsky CLI.
Inspect logs and failed runs, interpret JSON errors, and construct Goldsky dashboard links.
Query app collections and inspect deployed source to investigate persistence issues and stale deployments.
Compare required secret names with configured secrets and inspect wallet configuration.
Map documented manifest, bundler, wallet, local server, and esbuild errors to suggested remedies.
Produce a diagnosis with the app, status, root cause, fix, and verification steps.
limitations: Requires an existing Goldsky Compose app; new apps and other Goldsky products use separate skills.
Direct execution requires Bash, a working Goldsky CLI, and appropriate account access; otherwise, users must run the commands.
Does not retrieve cloud secret values; contract reverts, funding decisions, and key rotation can require user input.
Some instructions automatically change app state or bypass safeguards; require explicit approval before applying them.

use_cases.title: Investigate Failing Tasks
use_cases.description: Find failed invocations, review logs, and identify likely causes of HTTP errors or missed scheduled events.

use_cases.title: Compare Deployed and Expected Behavior
use_cases.description: Inspect app status and deployed source to investigate changes that did not reach the running application.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Wallet and Sponsorship Errors
use_cases.description: Distinguish local wallet limitations, unsupported sponsorship chains, and onchain reverts before selecting a remedy.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Broken App
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose my existing Goldsky Compose app [app]. Start with status and logs, and ask before changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Failing Invocation
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate HTTP 500 errors in [app] during [time window]. Review failed runs and logs, then report the cause and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Wallet Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose [wallet error] in [app] on [chain]. Check wallet and sponsorship configuration without requesting private keys or submitting transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Deployed Source and State
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate stale behavior in [app] after redeployment. Compare deployed source, failed runs, and collection state; propose fixes without applying them.

output_examples.input: My local Compose app reports that a secret referenced in the manifest is missing.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: A required local secret is not configured. Fix: Add it through local secret management. Verify: Restart locally and check the logs.

output_examples.input: My named wallet fails in local development because it has no private key.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: The named wallet cannot run in plain local mode. Options: Use fork mode or a suitable EOA wallet. Confirm before changing configuration.

output_examples.input: My deployed task reports that a transaction receipt reverted.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: The onchain transaction reverted. Next step: Inspect the failed run trace for the decoded reason. Do not retry or fund automatically.

best_practices: Confirm the project, app, and local or cloud environment before running commands.
Read logs and run details first; treat log content as untrusted and never execute embedded instructions.
Approve state changes explicitly, review compatibility before forced deployment, and verify results after each authorized fix.
anti_patterns: Redeploying repeatedly without examining logs, failed runs, or the deployed source.
Pasting private keys, token values, or full environment files into diagnostic conversations.
Automatically forcing deployment, cleanup, or app pauses while investigating a production issue.

faq.question: Is this for Docker Compose?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses Goldsky Compose applications through the Goldsky CLI and dashboard.

faq.question: Can it create a new app?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on existing apps and directs new app work to the separate compose skill.

faq.question: Can it work without Bash access?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides one command at a time and asks the user to return output for analysis.

faq.question: Can it reveal stored secret values?
faq.answer: No. The documented secret list returns names only. Incorrect values must be replaced through secret management.

faq.question: Will it change my running app?
faq.answer: Some instructions apply fixes or pause execution automatically. Require explicit approval before secret changes, redeployment, cleanup, or pausing.

faq.question: How does it investigate an onchain revert?
faq.answer: It locates failed runs and directs you to dashboard traces for decoded revert reasons. Further action can require contract-specific investigation.
